claims.token_machine: Five states, two tapes. Entry is canonical Tape.ofWord word plus pristine Tape.blank. For every finite Boolean word, exactly word.length+1 elapsed transitions reach state4, input <word.reverse.map bitSymbol,blank,[]> and token output <replicate b zero,blank,[]>.
claims.token_count: b = word.dropLast.length + indicator(word.dropLast.any id). For normalized word=compact bits, b=ceilLog2(wordValue bits) and for every natural k, b<=k iff wordValue bits<=2^k.
claims.power_of_two: ceilLog2 n is 0 for n=0; otherwise n.log2 plus zero when n=2^n.log2 and one otherwise. Zero and one explicitly produce b=0. Canonical positive bit length is not substituted for this parameter.
claims.arbitrary_word_boundary: Physical scan/count works for arbitrary word, but ceiling identification is only stated for compact bits. For example an all-zero noncanonical word of length2 emits one token despite numeric value0.
claims.binary_machine: Fifteen states, three tapes. Canonical word on slot0; slots1 and2 pristine. One actual tape-preserving bridge joins token scan to the unchanged automatic-width counter. At some t<=13*word.length+6, state14 is halted.
claims.final_slot2: <[],blank,r.map bitSymbol ++ [blank]>, r=(CarryTape.pass b (replicate b false)).1; r.length=b and wordValue r=b.
claims.empty_and_one: For word=[] and normalized one=[true], b=0. The binary record still has distinct represented home/end blanks; it is not a canonical one-cell blank output. Slot1 also has its represented left blank. No singleton-zero encoding is introduced.
